findings.body:
The change removes the `samples.is_empty()` guard from `fixture::average`. For an empty slice, `total` is 0 and `samples.len() as u32` is 0, so the integer division `total / 0` now runs and panics. Before the change, the function returned 0 early. The only in-repo caller, `report` at line 7, passes its slice straight through with no guard, so `report(&[])` now panics where it previously returned "mean=0".

Trigger: Calling `fixture::average(&[])` directly, or `fixture::report(&[])`, which forwards to `average`.

Impact: Public API callers that pass an empty slice to `average` or `report` now get a panic (division by zero) instead of 0 or "mean=0". Any caller that relied on the documented empty-input behaviour and has no try/catch-style guard can crash.
findings.suggestion: Restore the empty-slice guard: `if samples.is_empty() { return 0; }` before the division.
findings.title: average divides by zero on an empty slice after the empty guard was removed

risk_level.reason: The empty-slice guard was removed, so average now divides by zero and panics on empty input, and the public function has at least one caller elsewhere.
